item.title: Meet Google DeepMind’s Genie 4: Real-Time World Model With Native Audio
item.abstract: Google DeepMind has released Genie 4 as a research preview for trusted testers. The Genie 4 world model generates explorable worlds from text and image prompts in real time. It also generates the soundscape: ambient noise, music and character dialogue. Users move with keyboard controls and steer events with plain-language prompts. The bigger change is architectural. A Gemini model now runs inside the simulation loop as a planner. That pattern is important for anyone building training environments for agents or robots. Genie 4 is a world model from Google DeepMind that simulates interactive environments frame by frame. It is not a video clip generator. Each frame responds to user input as it arrives. DeepMind states that the model is natively multimodal . Audio, music and dialogue are generated together with the visuals. It is DeepMind’s first real-time world model to generate audio natively. It succeeds Genie 3 , announced in August 2025. Genie 3 ran at 720p and 24 frames per second, with visual memory reaching back 1 minute. Genie 4 borrows from 2 parts of the Gemini family. Gemini Omni anchors the look and behavior of each world. Other Gemini models handle the reasoning that keeps a simulation coherent. The runtime loop works like this: Between user inputs, Gemini also steers the scene so the world keeps progressing. DeepMind team frames this as an early step toward hybrid world models . In that design, a language model handles structure and narrative, while Genie renders pixels and sound. DeepMind released no benchmark tables for Genie 4. The comparison below uses only disclosed specs from each project’s own source. Genie 4 is live for trusted testers today. According to DeepMind, it is expected to be available soon to Google AI Ultra subscribers in Project Genie . Early access partners of the Gemini API and Google AI Studio come next. All Genie 4 video and audio will carry SynthID watermarks. DeepMind states that it ran internal safety evaluations before the preview. Testers so far span creative industries, journalism, education, gaming and engineering. DeepMind lists several open problems on the Genie 4 model page : Check out the Genie 4 announcement , the Genie 4 model page and the Project Genie waitlist . item.title: Meet LEANN: An Open-Source Vector Index that Shrinks a 60M-Chunk RAG Index from 201 GB to 6 GB
item.abstract: UC Berkeley’s Sky Computing Lab built LEANN , an open-source vector index that stores almost no embeddings. The LEANN vector index recomputes embeddings at query time instead of saving them to disk. The repo benchmark shows a 60 million chunk Wikipedia index dropping from 201 GB to 6 GB. The research paper won the Best Research Paper award at MLSys 2026 . So, it brings semantic search and RAG over personal data, on a laptop. LEANN is a low-storage approximate nearest neighbor (ANN) index built on top of FAISS . It targets one problem: vector indexes are often bigger than the data they index. The research paper shows a 76 GB corpus needs 173 GB of embeddings plus a 15 GB HNSW graph. That more than doubles the raw data. LEANN keeps a pruned graph, drops the full vectors, and rebuilds them on demand. The code is MIT licensed and installs with uv pip install leann . Graph indexes like HNSW visit only a small set of nodes per query. LEANN exploits that. It stores the graph plus a compact product quantization (PQ) table. At query time, it re-embeds only nodes on the search path. 3 techniques keep this practical: In ablations, two-level search gives an average 1.4x speedup. Adding batching raises it to 1.8x. Embedding recomputation still accounts for about 76% of query latency. The research team tested NQ, TriviaQA, GPQA and HotpotQA against a 60M-passage RPJ-Wiki datastore. Latency is measured at 90% Recall@3. All figures below are self-reported in the research paper . On NQ, with Qwen3-4B on an RTX 4090, LEANN and HNSW both reach 25.5% downstream accuracy. LEANN uses 4 GB of storage. HNSW uses 188 GB. BM25 scores 18.3%, and PQ compression scores 17.9%. The cost is search time. LEANN retrieval takes 2.48 s on NQ, versus 0.05 s for HNSW. Generation takes about 20 s, so end-to-end latency rises from 20.95 s to 23.34 s. Across datasets on the RTX 4090, LEANN retrieval ranges from 1.12 s (GPQA) to 7.12 s (HotpotQA). The IVF-based recomputation baseline, inspired by EdgeRAG , is up to 200x slower. LEANN improves exact match by up to 11.8% over BM25. The GitHub repo reports similar savings on personal data. 400K chat messages shrink from 1.8 GB to 64 MB. 38K browser entries shrink from 130 MB to 6.4 MB. Storage, latency and accuracy figures come from the LEANN paper v2 , Tables 1 and 2 and Section 7.2 (self-reported). License and design rows link to each project’s own source. The repo ships ready apps for documents, Apple Mail, Chrome history, WeChat, iMessage, and ChatGPT or Claude exports. MCP readers pull live data from Slack and Twitter bookmarks. LEANN also runs as a semantic search MCP server for Claude Code . On 30 SWE-Bench Pro tasks from ContextBench, the team reports 24.2% initial relevant-code recall versus 11.4% for BM25. The agent also used 8.4% fewer tokens. HNSW is the default backend, with DiskANN for faster search. Generation works with Ollama, Hugging Face, Anthropic, or any OpenAI-compatible API. It supports Ubuntu, Arch, WSL, macOS and Windows. Some apps, like Apple Mail search, are macOS only. Check out the Paper , GitHub Repo and PyPI package . item.title: Google DeepMind Introduces Gemini 4 Carbon, Its Top Model for Cyber Defense and Coding
item.abstract: Google DeepMind has introduced Gemini 4 Carbon , its strongest model to date. Gemini 4 Carbon is a frontier model from Google built for long-horizon agentic coding and cybersecurity defense. It ranks #1 on the updated v5.0 Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index with a score of 59. For developers, the catch is access. Carbon starts with a vetted group of cyber defenders, not the public API. Carbon is the second Gemini 4 model, following Gemini 4 Argon . Google team states that the model targets hard, long-running engineering work. Internal teams saw Carbon run for days on single tasks. Examples include root-causing and patching subtle bugs across large codebases and low-level systems. Google also tuned Carbon for full-stack web development and multimodal understanding. On WebDev Arena , Carbon gained 89 Elo points to reach #4 at 1769. Google published a 17-row comparison in its launch post . Carbon was run at the highest thinking setting. Most rival numbers are self-reported by each provider, per Google’s evaluation methodology . Agentic coding : Carbon scores 65.2% on Terminal-Bench 4.0 (AA), ahead of Opus 5.5 at 59.6%. It hits 9.6% on SWE-sweep, narrowly ahead of GPT-6 Astra at 9.5%. On FrontierSWE, GPT-6 Astra leads at 65.5% versus Carbon’s 61.2%. Computer use and knowledge work : Carbon reaches 77.4% on Agents’ Last Exam v1.1. On Vending-Bench 2, it ends with a $16,484 bank balance, the highest listed. Long context and science : GraphWalks is the widest gap: 96.2% versus 71.8% for GPT-6 Astra. Carbon also posts 80.0% on RiemannBench. Google frames Carbon around the full defense lifecycle: find, validate, then fix. Cyber benchmarks were evaluated without guardrails. Google computed SEC-bench Pro and ExploitGym scores itself, using its Antigravity harness. ExploitGym ran with mitigations off. Internally, Carbon showed more than 2x higher success at generating secure code than Argon. Google team states that the Chrome team found Carbon over 10x better than another lab’s model at high-quality patches. Wiz reports Carbon leading its web penetration testing benchmarks. Carbon keeps Argon’s layered stack: training, real-time misuse defenses, prompt-injection resilience and chain-of-thought monitoring. Google reports several alignment gains: These are Google’s internal or self-run figures. Independent replication is not yet available. Not yet, for most. Google is participating in the U.S. government’s voluntary pre-release testing process. This week, a subset of cyber defenders gets access. More trusted partners follow through the Fairwind Program , which prioritizes governments, critical infrastructure operators and core tech platforms. Developers, businesses and consumers get Carbon later, with no date given. Pricing matches Argon’s introductory rate: $2 per million input tokens and $10 per million output tokens. Cached input is 95% off. After the introductory period, prices rise to $4 and $20. Benchmark rows: Google launch post ; rival scores mostly self-reported per methodology . item.title: Polymathic AI and Princeton Researchers Release FlashMap, a Flow Map Drafter for 6.14x Faster LLM Decoding
item.abstract: Researchers from Polymathic AI, Princeton University, USC ISI, NYU and the Flatiron Institute have released FlashMap . FlashMap speculative decoding replaces the discrete diffusion drafter with a continuous flow map. It drafts a full 16-token block in 1 forward pass. Tokens in that block stay consistent with each other. On Qwen3-8B, the research team reports up to 6.14x lossless speedup on GSM8K. Drafter weights for Qwen3-8B and Qwen3-4B are on Hugging Face , with vLLM and SGLang plugins . FlashMap is a speculative decoding drafter that maps Gaussian noise to a token block in 1 step. A small drafter proposes K tokens. The target model then checks all K in 1 parallel pass and keeps the longest matching prefix. Output stays exactly what the target would produce. Speed depends on 2 things. How many drafted tokens get accepted, and how cheaply they were drafted. EAGLE-3 drafts autoregressively, so cost grows with block length. DFlash drafts the full block in 1 pass with block diffusion. DFlash predicts each slot in the block independently. The research team calls this the factorized approximation. Picture a continuation that is “new york” or “san diego” with equal odds. An independent drafter proposes “new diego” or “san york” half the time. The target rejects those at slot 2. FlashMap builds on Flow Map Language Models . Each noise sample maps to 1 full block. The noise picks the mode for every slot jointly. The drafter is a 6-block diffusion transformer (DiT), with embedding dimension 2048 and 16 attention heads. It reads hidden states from target layers 1, 9, 17, 25 and 33. Embedding matrix and LM head are copied from the target and stay frozen. Both drafters train on 500K samples from Open-PerfectBlend . Total compute across all models and ablations was about 4,600 GPU hours on H200s. The research team retrained EAGLE-3 and DFlash on the same data and settings. Tests cover 9 benchmarks across math, code and chat, at temperatures 0 and 1. A shuffle test checks whether drafts use real inter-token structure. At 2 steps, FlashMap recovers most of the joint-structure gain of a 16-step teacher. At 1 step, it keeps only a small fraction. Drafting 4 noise samples as a tree raised speedup by 11% on average. Average speedups are computed by Marktechpost from Figure 1(c) of the FlashMap paper. Matched rows use the authors’ retrained baselines. The flashmap package needs only torch and transformers>=4.56 . Install it with uv pip install flashmap . A spec_generate call runs drafter and target together on 1 GPU. For serving, the project page gives 2 paths: Set num_steps=2 to trade some speed for higher acceptance. For sampling above temperature 0, vLLM needs "draft_sample_method": "probabilistic" . item.title: Liquid AI Releases LFM3: 6 Open-Weight 2B-Class Multimodal Models
item.abstract: Liquid AI has released LFM3 , its new generation of Liquid Foundation Models. Liquid AI LFM3 is a family of 6 open-weight, 2B-class models built on one shared backbone. The family covers text, vision, audio, omni and decision tasks. Every model can be fine-tuned on a single GPU. Developers can then deploy on phones, laptops, private servers or the cloud. LFM3 is a multimodal model family from Liquid AI that branches 6 models from 1 base. All of them start from LFM3-1.7B-Base . The backbone mixes 3 operators across 24 layers . There are 13 gated short convolutions, 5 sliding-window attention layers and 6 global attention layers. The SWA window is 256 tokens. Convolution kernels grew from 3 to 7. Liquid AI team found this mix with its hardware-in-the-loop architecture search. LFM2 was tuned on 1 phone and 1 laptop. LFM3 was tuned across 14 device and backend combinations. These include a Raspberry Pi 5 and the Qualcomm Hexagon NPU. Other changes include head-wise sigmoid gates on attention, partial RoPE on global layers and sandwich norm. The base model saw 22T tokens. The last 3.5T tokens were agent-heavy mid-training, which also extended context to 256K. Post-training ran in 4 stages. SFT on 1.75T tokens came first, then mixed RL. Next, 6 specialist teachers were distilled into 1 model, followed by agentic RL. Liquid AI reports that LFM3-1.7B beats LFM2.5-2.6B with 35% fewer parameters. The bigger story is the agent results. On WebArena-Verified it scores 38.42, against 28.94 for Qwen3.5-9B. On BFCL V4 it scores 71.39, against 62.83. Size still wins on knowledge and agentic coding. GPQA Diamond is 63.37, versus 80.40 for Qwen3.5-9B. SWE-bench Verified is 43.40, versus 51.20. Search narrows the gap: Humanity’s Last Exam rises from 7.17 to 13.90 with tools. Sources: Liquid LFM3 model card , MiniCPM5-2B card , Qwen3.5-4B card , Gemma 4 E4B card , LFM license . LFM3-VL-2B averages 71.4 across 62 vision benchmarks. Gemma 4 12B scores 71.7 on the same suite. It leads that comparison on visual grounding (77.3) and GUI understanding (83.1). Video (61.2) and agentic tasks (42.5) still trail larger API models. LFM3-Audio-2B reaches 6.2 English WER and a 3.8 UTMOSv2 TTS score. LFM3-Omni-2B scores 70.1 on Daily-Omni, against 61.3 for Qwen2.5-Omni-7B. d1-2B replaces d1-3B with a third fewer parameters. It improves Decision Bench from 83.6 to 85.2. Weights are on Hugging Face , the Liquid AI Playground and the Liquid API. The docs list GGUF, MLX and ONNX for the text and vision models. Runtimes include llama.cpp, MLX, vLLM, SGLang, Ollama and Transformers. On-device, Liquid AI measured llama.cpp at Q4_0 with 32K context. A full 128K context needs 1.6 GB of KV cache. Qwen3.5-4B needs 4.3 GB. On 1 NVIDIA B300 with SGLang, LFM3-1.7B produces 3.6B tokens per day at 1,024 concurrent requests. Liquid AI also showed specialization. A few hours of SFT and GRPO on 1 A100 lifted wind-turbine defect classification to 67%. Check out the technical details , model weights and docs . item.title: KV Cache被壓成常數！OCR開源新王：頁數沒上限，快取砍96%
item.abstract: KV Cache被壓成常數！OCR開源新王：頁數沒上限，快取砍96% 聽雨 2026-10-27 16:35:33 來源： 量子位 OCR 3.0時代，來了 聽雨 發自 凹非寺 量子位 | 公眾號 QbitAI 百度的OCR又升級了， 文心Unlimited OCR 2正式釋出並開源！ 這次，它直接挑戰一口氣讀完整套小說。 7部《哈利·波特》，從《魔法石》到《死亡聖器》，連續識別、轉寫，3600+頁一路讀到最後。 換成《三體》全集，同樣能一口氣讀完，三本書1200+頁，幾十萬字，中間也不帶喘的。 不過，連著讀這麼多頁，模型得先過一道關： 視訊記憶體 。 文件越長，推理時需要保留的中間資訊（KV快取）就越多——可以理解為模型邊讀邊記的小抄，頁數越多，小抄越厚。小抄厚重，不光佔地方，翻起來也慢。 在技術報告的百頁級單序列測試中，文心Unlimited OCR 2給出了一組對比： 峰值KV快取佔用從標準解碼（將所有頁面的視覺快取同時保留在視訊記憶體中）的 47GB降至1.77GB，一口氣減少了約96%。 47GB是什麼概念？比不少筆記型電腦的整機記憶體還大。而這還只是KV快取，模型權重等其他開銷另算。 它的上一代Unlimited OCR，已經憑藉多頁文件連續解析能力，在開源社群積累了相當的人氣：累計下載量超過1000萬，在GitHub上收穫約2.86萬Star。 從社群製作線上Demo，到支援SGlang推理，圍繞它的適配也在持續推進。 到了第二代，升級重點在於連續處理更長文件的同時，把計算和快取負擔降下來。 為此，文心Unlimited OCR 2提出 稀疏參考滑動視窗注意力機制SR-SWA ，讓模型按需選取相關頁面和視覺資訊，減少重複計算。 配合持續解碼機制，模型能夠連續處理超長文件，單步解碼開銷也不會隨著文件變長而水漲船高。 目前，文心Unlimited OCR 2已在Hugging Face和GitHub正式開源。 開源地址： *GitHub ： https:// github.com/baidu/Unlimi ted-OCR* *HuggingFace ： https:// huggingface.co/baidu/Un limited-OCR-2* 拆解核心技術：SR-SWA怎麼少算，分塊解碼怎麼少存 連續讀完幾百萬字、3600+頁的《哈利波特》全集，文心Unlimited OCR 2究竟是怎麼做到的？ 它借鑑的，其實是人類抄書的思路。 人手抄書時是什麼流程？看一段、抄一段，眼睛主要盯著正在抄的那一頁；只有遇到需要前後對照的地方，才回頭翻一翻相關頁面。 抄書這件事，人類比模型更早就想明白了：沒人會一邊抄《論語》，一邊在腦子裡同時把《論語》全部頁數攤開一起看。 但上一代Unlimited OCR不是這麼幹的：雖然通過R-SWA已大幅降低推理階段的KV快取，但再回看的過程中，所有輸入頁面的視覺資訊依舊都要參與注意力計算。 文件越長，算的資訊越多，而其中相當一部分，跟當前正在識別的那幾行字壓根沒關係——典型的「陪跑」。 △SR-SWA借鑑人類抄書時的局部聚焦方式 順著人類抄書的思路，文心Unlimited OCR 2引入了 稀疏參考滑動視窗注意力機制（SR-SWA） 。 它的篩選分兩層：先把需要參考的頁面篩出來，再從篩出來的頁面裡挑出真正相關的局部資訊，把無關計算擋在門外。 從整體架構看，文心Unlimited OCR 2延續了上一代的基礎設計。 △文心Unlimited OCR 2整體架構 書頁影像先進入DeepEncoder，被轉成模型能處理的視覺Token——可以理解成一組記錄頁面內容與版面特徵的資料卡片。 接著，語言模型根據這些卡片，一步一步生成識別結果。 關鍵變化就發生在語言模型內部：上一代採用的 參考滑動視窗注意力機制（R-SWA） ，在這一代升級為SR-SWA。 架構圖中左下方展示的，就是SR-SWA的兩層篩選過程。 第一層是Page Gate，管「該看哪幾頁」。 它根據模型當前解析到的位置，把候選視覺資訊收攏到相關頁面範圍內，不讓無關頁面來湊熱鬧。 放到抄書的場景裡，就像讀到某一頁時，先找到與這一頁相關的幾個頁面，而不是從頭翻遍整本書。 第二層是Token Sieve，管「這一頁裡該看哪幾行」。 選對頁面只是第一步：即使在這些頁面中，也不必讓所有視覺Token都參與計算。Token Sieve會再做一次篩選，從頁面裡挑出與當前內容更相關的視覺資訊塊，以捕捉長距離視覺依賴關係。 架構圖右側展開了這一過程：先用各個資訊塊的簡要表示算出相關性，再通過TopK挑出得分最高、數量固定的資訊塊。 挑完之後，模型仍然會去看這些塊中的具體視覺資訊，而不是隻看個摘要。 兩層機制配合，讓模型既能在長文件中找到相關頁面，又能減少每一步需要處理的視覺資訊，從而提升長文件解析效率。 △Token Sieve細節 篩選出的視覺資訊，還會與圖中的 Local Window （局部滑動視窗）一起參與解析。 這個視窗大小固定，裝著最近的上下文，並隨著生成過程一路向前平移，負責讓模型順著剛才的內容往下寫。 資訊塊數量固定，局部視窗大小也固定，每一步需要參考的資訊量就被框住了——文件再長，這一步還是這麼多活兒。不會出現「書越厚、每寫一個字越費勁」的情況。 SR-SWA負責的是每一步少算點；而視訊記憶體裡到底要留多少資訊，則是另一個問題。 每頁影像經過編碼，都會變成一組視覺Token。模型生成解析結果時要參考它們，因此會存下對應的KV快取，供後續計算複用。 如果一次性讀入整份文件，再把所有頁面的視覺快取都留在視訊記憶體裡，頁數越多、佔的地方越大。 更麻煩的是：哪怕這些頁面根本沒參與當前計算，只要快取沒釋放，它們照樣佔著視訊記憶體不走。這就好比抄書時把每頁草稿都攤在桌上，一頁不扔——桌子再大也不夠用。 所以，少算一些，還得配合少存一些。 文心Unlimited OCR 2為此引入了 無限解碼機制 （Unlimited-Horizon Decoding Paradigm），通過分塊處理控制快取佔用。 △分塊解碼示意圖 item.title: Building an Agentic AI Platform on Amazon Bedrock AgentCore
item.abstract: If you’ve tried to get an agent into production, the model and tool use are not the blocker. The main bottleneck is everything around them: how many teams can build within a secure environment, which team owns each model and tool, how AgentOps and error handling stay inside a pre-defined boundary, and how platform, Workstream, and finance teams see cost and health across accounts. For a Platform team that wants to support many agentic use cases, that’s a platform product to design and operate. In this post, we refer to the team that manages the platform as the Platform team, and to the teams that build on it as Workstream teams. Workstream teams are the domain or product teams that build and own agents on the platform. Each Workstream team needs a paved road with approved models and tools, short-lived workload identity, isolated runtime and memory, automated evaluation, rollback, telemetry, and cost attribution. These controls need to remain consistent as Workstream teams customize prompts, tools, data access, and application behavior. When every team assembles them, controls drift, shared services become a bottleneck, and ownership is difficult to audit. In this post, we walk through the architecture and reference implementation of an enterprise Agentic AI Platform on Amazon Bedrock and Amazon Bedrock AgentCore. We cover the multi-account operating model, the Platform control plane, a repeatable per-Workstream deployment pattern, separate inference and tool gateways, and an evaluation pipeline that gates each agent before promotion to production. By the end, you should be able to deploy a governed Workstream from the companion blueprint, validate its security and lifecycle contracts, and use it as the foundation for your own agentic AI platform in the organization. Amazon Bedrock AgentCore provides modular services for building, deploying, and operating agents at scale, including runtime, gateway, identity, memory, policy, registry, and evaluations. The Enterprise Agentic AI Platform Blueprint , built on AgentCore, adds the surrounding enterprise contracts as deployable infrastructure as code: ownership, account boundaries, software delivery, observability, cost governance, and retirement. Before diving into the solution details, it helps to understand the organizational needs that drive the platform architecture. The common challenges we have heard from customers who establish an agent platform fall into these five categories: The blueprint addresses these needs through four connected planes: developer experience, platform control, Workstream execution, and assurance and operations. The unit of scale is the Workstream cell, not a manually configured agent or one shared workload account. The blueprint README documents the responsibilities of each plane in detail. And you will read the main planes: Agentic AI Platform control plane and Repeatable Workstream cell in the later paragraphs. Enterprises usually adopt one of three operating models for agentic AI: Following patterns we have observed in customer engagements, the blueprint implements the federated model. The Platform team is the hub, typically a Platform product manager, architect, platform engineers, agent operations engineers, and a security and governance lead. Workstream teams are the spokes, made up of agent developers, a domain tech lead, and AI/ML engineers. An executive sponsor and the CISO sit above both. In this blueprint, the Platform team owns the definition of each component: templates, versions, policies, and admission. Each Workstream account runs its own instance of the per-team components (Runtime, Memory, Tool Gateway), so a failure or rollback stays inside one team’s boundary. This solution delivers a governed, multi-account Agentic AI Platform that platform teams operate, and workstream teams such as internal product and engineering teams consume through versioned, self-service interfaces. At enterprise scale, the developer experience plane is a catalog of organization-approved, versioned agent templates. The blueprint ships reference templates for Strands , LangGraph , and CrewAI , but you can use your choice of framework when the template preserves the same inference gateway, tool gateway, identity, policy, evaluation, and delivery contracts. Application teams own prompts, agent logic, tools, and evaluation cases. The Platform team owns the common controls and release requirements. Out of the four planes, two carry most of the architecture: The following diagram illustrates the operating model and governed flow of the solution. Figure 1: Enterprise Agentic AI Platform operating model, showing the governance foundation, the Platform control plane, repeatable team-owned Workstream cells, and the software delivery, inference, tool, telemetry, and ownership flows between them. The architecture consists of the following account layers: The following sections trace the key design decisions: account topology, preventive and detective controls, the AgentCore execution path, and the delivery pipeline. The blueprint defines logical account roles that separate enterprise governance, shared Platform services, and team-owned execution: This topology integrates into an existing landing zone, a pre-configured, secure, and scalable multi-account AWS environment, where the Management, Platform, and Workstream labels describe responsibilities rather than a fixed three-account estate. An organization can operate multiple validated Platform environments and many Workstream account pairs. Start with one representative cell and prove onboarding, production promotion, rollback, centralized observability, and zero-residual retirement before repeating the baseline. Service control policies constrain the maximum permissions available to Platform and Workstream accounts. They complement, rather than replace, IAM, gateway authorization, Guardrails, resource policies, network controls, and pipeline evidence. The blueprint renders and reviews the effective policies for the exact account and Region instead of relying on source-code intent alone. An administrator inside a Workstream account can’t create a supported fast path around these controls. New or changed organization policies need a sandbox or representative-cell soak, exact allow and deny tests, and a rollback plan before broad attachment. The blueprint uses reviewed Platform and Workload pipelines to enforce the following promotion sequence: No Workstream deployment step has a manual fast track. The Platform team owns the release contract, but Workstream teams operate their own pipeline instances and deployment cadence. Retirement follows a strict dependency order: Platform alias grants are revoked first, then Workstream Gateway and tool roles, then Runtime, Memory, and application resources. Each step is verified before proceeding, and a final inventory confirms zero residual resources remain. The blueprint implements defense in depth through reinforcing identity, policy, delivery, data, and evidence controls: The repository is a reference implementation. Developers can adjust it to address their needs. The deployment and available features are based on the eu-west-1 (Ireland) Region. A substituted component, another Region, or a wider organizational rollout requires its own availability, security, load, rollback, observability, and teardown evidence. In this post, we walked through an enterprise Agentic AI Platform built on Amazon Bedrock AgentCore. The architecture separates a centrally governed Platform control plane from repeatable, team-owned Workstream cells, with distinct inference and tool gateways, and production promotion gated by deployed-runtime evaluation. The companion repository includes a blueprint that validates these controls end to end, from pipeline gates and adversarial boundary tests through zero-residual teardown. The support claim stops at that tested boundary.

item.title: Introducing LFM3: Every Modality for Specialized Intelligence
item.abstract:
Today, we’re excited to announce LFM3 , our new generation of Liquid Foundation Models (LFMs) built for specialized intelligence. The LFM3 model family is multimodal by nature and brings text, vision, audio, omni, and decision models onto one new shared backbone. The first release of the LFM3 family covers models in the 2B parameter range. Built on a new hybrid architecture and 22T tokens of pre-training, LFM3 is far more expressive than LFM2 while maintaining its efficiency. The extra capacity in a small, fast model makes LFM3 the ideal starting point in its class for specialized intelligence: this is because it can be fine-tuned locally, it can run on any device, and it is capable enough to become a reliable expert on a specialized task. The base and post-trained models are open-weight and available today on Hugging Face , our Playground , and the Liquid AI API . Check out our docs on how to run and fine-tune them locally. Download weights Try in Liquid API Try in Playground Benchmark in Pipette New architecture for more expressivity LFM2 showed that a hybrid of short convolutions and attention could run fast on-device without sacrificing quality. Its design came from our automated hardware-in-the-loop architecture search . For LFM3, we used this search to redesign that architecture for agentic use cases, which need more capability per parameter and fast inference over long contexts. We also expanded the hardware in the loop, from CPUs in one phone and one laptop for LFM2 to 14 device and backend combinations for LFM3: phones (Samsung Galaxy S26 Ultra and OnePlus 15), a Raspberry Pi 5, laptops (Apple M4 Max and AMD Ryzen AI), and Arm and x86 cloud CPUs, plus GPUs and the Qualcomm Hexagon NPU. Gated short convolutions still make up over half the layers. To add capability without slowing down long contexts, we tried swapping some of them for other sequence blocks, and sliding-window attention (SWA) gave the best quality–speed tradeoff. We kept the other changes described below only where they improved quality without a meaningful speed cost. The payoff shows at long context. Per parameter, LFM3-1.7B matches LFM2-1.2B on short prompts across edge devices, and with 8K tokens in context it is about 25% faster. Tri-hybrid layer mix. LFM3 combines three operators: gated short convolutions, sliding-window attention (SWA), and global attention. Of its 24 layers, 13 are convolutions, 5 are SWA with a 256-token window, and 6 are global attention. The convolutions also use a kernel size of 7, up from 3 in LFM2. Head-wise gated attention. A sigmoid gate scales each head’s output, so a head can switch off when it has nothing to add. This can help suppress activation outliers that hurt quantization and improve training stability . Partial RoPE. Global attention layers rotate only the highest-frequency half of each head and leave the low-frequency half unrotated, so those dimensions match on content regardless of distance . SWA layers keep full RoPE. Sandwich norm. Each block normalizes both its input and its output, which helps keep activations well-scaled. LFM3 uses the same 128K vocabulary as LFM2.5-8B-A1B , built to tokenize non-Latin scripts more efficiently. Training. LFM3-1.7B-Base was pre-trained on 22T tokens. Compared with LFM2, the mix adds more scientific papers, repository-level code, a wider range of knowledge sources, and considerably more math. The final 3.5T tokens are a mid-training stage on curated, higher-quality data, with a larger share of agentic traces and diverse tool calls to prepare the model for agentic post-training. This stage also extends the context window to 256K tokens. A multimodal family for every need The first LFM3 release includes six models, all branched from the same LFM3-1.7B-Base backbone and all around 2B parameters. Four of them cover different input modalities (text, vision, audio, and omni), and the last two are decision models specialized from the vision and omni models. Instead of running one large general-purpose model, you can pick the one that fits your use case, customize it, and run it on-device. For a deeper dive into the performance and inference results behind these models, refer to the respective model cards. “ As AI increasingly moves from the cloud to the client, developers need models that can be deployed efficiently across the broad spectrum of AI PCs. Liquid AI's LFM3 family combines strong multimodal capabilities with a compact footprint that is well suited for on-device AI experiences. AMD has worked closely with Liquid AI across multiple generations of models, and we're excited to see LFM3 expand what's possible for specialized AI applications running locally on systems with AMD Ryzen™ AI processors. Josh Hort Senior Director & Head of ISV Enabling at AMD Across industries, we’re seeing edge AI evolve from running dedicated detection and perception models to supporting multiple concurrent AI workloads, including vision-language models, natural-language interfaces and multimodal reasoning. The challenge is delivering these capabilities within the compute, memory, and power constraints of edge devices. LFM3 brings text, vision, and audio together in a unified architecture designed for efficient deployment, with open weights that developers can fine-tune for specific applications. Developers can already run Liquid AI’s LFM2.5-VL models on Ambarella silicon through the Cooper Model Garden, and we have begun enabling LFM3 on the same platform. Malhar Palkar Senior Director for AI at Ambarella The next generation of AI will be more multimodal, personalized, and private while being distributed across devices and the cloud. Liquid AI’s LFM3 family is an exciting step in that direction, and we’re pleased to work together to bring fast, efficient, and innovative AI experiences to devices powered by Snapdragon® processors. Vinesh Sukumar VP, Qualcomm Technologies, Inc. 01 / 03 Text LFM3-1.7B is a text model for local agents and specialized applications with a 256K-token context window. It is post-trained to run in agentic harnesses such as Hermes Agent, Pi, and OpenClaw. It can triage your inbox, manage your calendar, research topics on the web, send you morning briefings on WhatsApp, and use tool search to find the right tool among thousands of options. Since tokens are free, dozens of agents can run continuously in the background. You can adapt it to your domains, harnesses, and tools with a short fine-tuning run on a single GPU. item.abstract: MiniMax has open-sourced MCode Stack , the workflows and agent skills its team uses to build MiniMax Code. The MiniMax MCode Stack agent skills went public on October 28, 2026 under the MIT license . It is not a prompt collection. Each piece is a SKILL.md skill or checklist that installs directly into MiniMax Code . For developers, it turns harness engineering habits into steps an agent can actually run. We just open-sourced MCode Stack: the actual workflows and skills the MiniMax Code team uses every day to build MiniMax Code. https://t.co/vREt7i8m2M MCode Stack is an open-source repo of agent skills from MiniMax’s MiniMax Code team. MiniMax Code is the MiniMax’s open-source terminal coding agent, also MIT-licensed. The stack holds no MiniMax Code source code. It holds only workflows, skills and checklists. The repo pairs with a column called MCode Engineering Notes . Each note explains one idea. The repo makes that idea runnable. Published notes cover subagents , tool context , compaction versus memory and long bash commands . A note on per-turn context tax is marked upcoming. MiniMax’s stack ships 15 skills, grouped by moment in the working day: A few ideas stand out. independent-review gives the reviewer exactly 3 inputs: the diff, the requirement and test results. It deliberately withholds the author’s conversation. The reasoning: a reviewer inheriting the author’s context repeats the author’s blind spots. The 6 engineering-* skills are adapted from Google Engineering Practices . That material stays under CC-BY 3.0, per the stack’s NOTICE . There are 3 paths, per the README : The same catalog works in Claude Code with /plugin marketplace add MiniMax-AI/mcode-stack . MiniMax Code also reads ~/.claude/skills/ and ~/.codex/skills/ . The skills use the common SKILL.md format, so most work in other agents that support skills. MCode Stack is narrower than both. It targets people who design agent harnesses, not only people who use agents. Superpowers covers far more harnesses today. Check out the GitHub repo and MiniMax Code . item.title: NVIDIA Nemotron 3.5 Transcribe and Granary v2: Intelligent Multilingual Transcription You Can Prompt and Adapt
item.abstract: Back to Articles NVIDIA Nemotron 3.5 Transcribe and Granary v2: Intelligent Multilingual Transcription You Can Prompt and Adapt Enterprise + Article Published October 28, 2026 Upvote 34 +28 Maryam Motamedi maryameee Follow nvidia Piotr Żelasko piotrzelasko Follow nvidia Kunal Dhawan kunaldhawan Follow nvidia Nikolay Karpov nkarpov Follow nvidia Nune Tadevosyan nunetadevosyan Follow nvidia Meline Mkrtchyan mmkrtchyan Follow nvidia Nithin Rao Koluguri nithinraok Follow nvidia Francesco fciannella Follow nvidia One open model for multilingual transcription, speaker attribution, translation, and audio Q&A, with top leaderboard results, plus the open Granary v2 data pipeline and fine-tuning recipes to adapt it. A transcript can capture every spoken word and still leave users or applications wondering who said what, how to translate it, or how to format domain-specific jargon. Multilingual calls, fast-paced meetings, and medical dictation each need different output: a translation, speaker labels, or correctly spelled medical terms. NVIDIA Nemotron 3.5 Transcribe is an open-weight, promptable model that turns recorded speech into useful text, now available on Hugging Face and ModelScope . It brings transcription, speaker attribution (diarization), translation, and audio question answering into one checkpoint: it transcribes 40 languages, translates 31 of them to or from English, and attributes speakers in 13. It handles recordings up to an hour long and labels up to eight speakers. Developers can guide output with natural language, choose where their audio is processed, and adapt recognition to domain vocabulary and accents. Transcribe is first among open-weight models on the Hugging Face Open ASR Leaderboard for English and sits on Artificial Analysis ’s accuracy–active-parameter frontier. For speaker attribution, it posts the lowest error rate on David AI’s 21-language diarization leaderboard and ranks first in VoiceArena’s 14-system comparison . Quantized versions are coming soon, so you can run Transcribe locally on your RTX Spark, DGX Spark, or Jetson AGX Thor—or scale up on Blackwell data-center GPUs. Granary v2’s multilingual data (available on Hugging Face and ModelScope ) and reusable curation pipeline, together with NeMo Speech fine-tuning tools , extend prompt-level control to training: developers can define the written form they need and adapt the model to the speech their applications encounter. In a medical case study , fine-tuning cut word error rate (WER) on held-out speakers by 45.8% relative to the best prompt. Guide transcription and analysis with natural language The same checkpoint can turn one meeting recording into different outputs, depending on the instruction: “Transcribe this recording and label each speaker.” “Translate this audio into English.” “What decisions were made in this meeting?” Experience the model in action in the video below, where it tackles a classic scene from the 1940 screwball comedy His Girl Friday—a film famous for its rapid-fire, heavily overlapping dialogue. Nemotron 3.5 Transcribe captions a scene from His Girl Friday (1940) and labels speakers, including overlapping dialogue. For unfamiliar terms, try context before training. In a healthcare setting, for example: Transcribe this medical discussion in the original language. Possible terms: HbA1c, metformin. Use these terms only when supported by the audio. Preserve standard medical spelling and write numbers in conventional written form. The model card has recommended presets, including reasoning for audio questions, plus the full prompt guide and a task-by-language matrix: language support differs by task, and audio question answering is trained in English. Word-level timestamps are also supported. As with any speech model, spot-check names, speaker changes, and answers against the recording. From live classes to lasting lessons. Agora, whose real-time voice and video platform powers live conversations in apps, used word-level timestamps in a classroom demo: Nemotron 3.5 Transcribe turns a recorded class into a transcript shown alongside the replay, so students can see what was said and when. Agora’s blog walks through how they built it. Leaderboard wins from transcription to speaker attribution Among open-weight models, Transcribe leads on what was said; on who said it, it tops two speaker-attribution benchmarks outright. Hugging Face Open ASR Leaderboard. The leaderboard measures transcription accuracy as word error rate (WER) on public test sets, in three tracks: English: first among open-weight models at 5.33% average WER (Figure 1). Multilingual: 4.62% mean WER across seven languages, the lowest among evaluated open-weight models in the model card’s Open ASR comparison. Long-form: 10.98% mean WER, also the lowest in that comparison. Figure 1. Nemotron 3.5 Transcribe ranks first among open-weight models on the Hugging Face Open ASR Leaderboard (English) at 5.33% average WER, with API models excluded. Lower WER means fewer transcription errors. Artificial Analysis Speech-to-Text Leaderboard. Artificial Analysis independently ranks speech-to-text models by AA-WER, its word error rate index. Nemotron 3.5 Transcribe ties for first among open-weight models at 2.8% AA-WER, with about 4B active parameters versus 24B for the model it ties. On AA-AgentTalk, the held-out voice-agent speech set that makes up 50% of the AA-WER index, Transcribe scores 1.8% WER, versus 2.3% for the next-best open-weight model. Transcribe pairs its speech encoder with a hybrid Mamba–Transformer mixture-of-experts language model, so only about 4B of its 30B parameters are active per token. That puts it on Artificial Analysis ’s open-weight Pareto frontier of accuracy versus active parameters. On AA’s all-model chart, it ranks ahead of several widely used proprietary speech APIs. Figure 2. Leading AA accuracy at about one-sixth the active parameters: Nemotron 3.5 Transcribe achieves 2.80% AA-WER with approximately 4B active parameters. Speaker attribution across languages and overlap. Sortformer speaker cues reach the language model with the acoustic features, so Transcribe can tag each turn during generation instead of relying solely on a later step to attach speakers to words. David AI DAI-ASR-I18N Leaderboard. On David AI’s DAI-ASR-I18N combined transcription-and-speaker-attribution track , Transcribe ranks first among evaluated open-weight models and second overall. On the benchmark’s diarization track, which scores who spoke when across 21 languages, it has the lowest diarization error rate of the 14 systems tested, slightly ahead of NVIDIA’s dedicated Nemotron 3 Diarization model. Figure 3. NVIDIA models hold the top two spots on David AI’s multilingual diarization leaderboard : Nemotron 3.5 Transcribe posts the lowest overall diarization error rate (DER), 18.26% across 21 languages, followed by Nemotron 3 Diarization at 18.38%. DER measures speaker-time errors; lower is better. VoiceArena Diarization-Bench. On VoiceArena’s English full-session benchmark , Transcribe posts the lowest concatenated minimum-permutation WER (cpWER) of 14 systems and ranks first in both in-person and online settings. It also drops the fewest words: deletions are 8.32% of reference words, versus a median of about 31%. Figure 4. NVIDIA models hold the top two spots in VoiceArena’s 14-system comparison : Nemotron 3.5 Transcribe leads at 32.4% cpWER, followed by NVIDIA Multitalker Parakeet with Nemotron 3 Diarization at 34.2%. Diarization-Bench v1 covers English full sessions, overlapping speech and 2–8 speakers. cpWER counts word errors after matching speaker labels; lower is better. More evaluations. Ocular AI’s Converse-STT evaluation ranks Transcribe the top open model. Josh Talks’ Voice of India leaderboard reports Transcribe’s results across Indian languages. High-throughput transcription.

item.title: OXR強勢開源！1.3B橫掃全球三榜第一，速度快過Paddle、MinerU，RSI讓它卷出新高度
item.abstract: OXR強勢開源！1.3B橫掃全球三榜第一，速度快過Paddle、MinerU，RSI讓它卷出新高度 量子位的朋友們 2026-10-27 15:41:02 來源： 量子位 開源一週，Github 拿下超 1000 star，X上關注度破百萬，並登上 Today‘s news 推薦 文件解析賽道，又迎來一位強勁的新選手。 OXR 正式開源：主模型僅 1.3B 參數，在 OmniDocBench、olmOCR-Bench 和 DocParsingBench 三項基準測試中全部登頂，完整解析速度也超過了同場參測的 PaddleOCR-VL-1.6 和 MinerU2.5-Pro，把輕量模型的精度與效率同時推到了榜首。 其背後的 SoMark 團隊來自國內一家初創公司，深耕於文件智慧領域，此前持續圍繞核心產品 SoMark 打磨解析能力，如今推出了開源模型 OXR。 OXR 的全稱是 Optical Everything Recognition ，從 OCR 到 OXR，OXR 要處理的遠不止文字。它能夠解析表格、公式、化學式等 13 類文件元素，準確還原多欄版面的閱讀順序，輸出 Markdown / JSON，並保留版面座標，讓複雜文件成為 Agent 可以繼續使用的資料。 1 高精度解析，全球三榜第一 根據團隊公佈的評測結果， OXR 在 OmniDocBench、olmOCR-Bench 和 DocParsingBench 上分別取得 97.18、87.84 和 87.76 分，均位列第一。 分數之外，更直觀的是看 OXR 如何處理複雜文件。 一張跨行跨列的表格，文字識別正確只是第一步。行列關係或合併單元格一旦錯位，數字就可能對應到錯誤的專案。OXR 可以保留這些結構，並將表格輸出為 HTML，供後續展示和處理。 科研文件裡的難點則更密集：數學公式有上下標和巢狀結構，化學內容還有反應式與分子結構圖。OXR 將公式輸出為 LaTeX，化學方程式用 mhchem 表示，化學結構式用 SMILES 表示，讓這些內容從頁面上的圖形變成可繼續處理的表達。 多欄論文、報紙和試卷還考驗閱讀順序。即便每個區域都識別正確，左右欄串讀、正文與旁註混雜，仍會破壞原文含義。OXR 在識別內容的同時判斷閱讀順序，並提供版面座標，保留內容在頁面中的位置。 這些能力共同構成了 OXR 的“Everything”：覆蓋文字、表格、公式、化學結構式、程式碼塊等 13 類文件元素，將 PDF 和文件圖片解析為 Markdown / JSON，供 Agent、RAG 等下游流程使用。 2 精度與速度雙 SOTA：不只準，而且快 處理單份文件，幾秒的差異未必明顯；當任務變成批次論文入庫、檔案整理或研報解析，處理效率就會直接影響等待時間與算力佔用。 根據團隊公佈的同條件完整解析測試結果，在同一張 RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell（96GB）顯示卡上，解析從 OmniDocBench 隨機抽取的 100 頁文件， OXR 平均用時約 101 秒，PaddleOCR-VL-1.6 和 MinerU2.5-Pro 則分別需要約 145 秒和 255 秒。 小參數、高精度、快速度，這次出現在了同一個模型上。 這得益於OXR 在任務分工上做的一個巧妙設計： 由輕量版面分析模型定位內容區域，再由主模型完成內容識別與閱讀順序判斷。 把排序併入內容識別階段，減少了單獨處理閱讀順序的額外開銷，也讓模型能夠結合內容語義判斷先後關係。這是 OXR 兼顧解析質量與效率 的一項架構設計。 3 RSI：圍繞錯樣本和弱樣本持續改進 耀眼的成績背後，OXR 的訓練思路同樣值得看。我們都知道，文件解析很難靠一套固定樣本覆蓋所有問題。場景、語言、版式不斷變化，如何讓模型面對沒見過的複雜文件，也能穩定輸出可靠的解析結果呢？ OXR 創新性地 在後訓練階段首次引入面向文件解析的遞迴自我改進（Recursive Self-Improvement，RSI） 訓練範式，將解析中的錯樣本和弱樣本轉化為下一輪訓練的依據。 這套流程可以理解為一次由多個 AI 模型協作完成的“查錯與補課”： OXR 先解析無標籤文件，產生待評估的結果。 外部模型評判結果、逐樣本分析錯誤原因，獨立聚類模型將問題按原因歸類。 外部模型圍繞這些問題定向生成訓練資料，用於下一輪 OXR 訓練。 這樣一來，訓練資料的準備就有了明確的問題指向：模型哪裡薄弱，就圍繞哪裡補充資料，加快了模型迭代的步伐。同時， 閉環中新增加的訓練資料無需人工標註， 也突破了人工準備材料帶來的效率瓶頸。 4 版面分析可插拔，業務適配更靈活 模型讀錯了，需要提高準確率；但很多時候，解析結果不符合預期，是因為業務對文件結構有不同的定義。 例如，同一組圖片，資料歸檔可能希望整體保留，圖片檢索則需要逐張提取；一個包含標題、文字和邊框的區域，有的業務按文本拆分，有的業務希望整體作為表格處理。兩種需求都可能合理。 對此，OXR 將版面分析設計為獨立、可插拔模組。 你可以直接使用內建版面分析模型，也可以接入符合自身業務標準的其他版面分析模型，調整元素類別、區域邊界與內容分組，再繼續複用 OXR 的內容識別和閱讀順序判斷能力。 對於構建 RAG、Agent 和文件工作流的開發者，OXR 無疑提供了一個兼顧解析精度、處理速度與版面適配能力的開源選擇。 目前，OXR 已開放程式碼與模型權重，並提供線上 Demo 和免費 API，方便開發者直接用真實文件檢驗效果： GitHub 程式碼倉庫：https://github.com/SoMarkAI/OXR Hugging Face 模型權重：https://huggingface.co/SoMarkAI/OXR-1.0 線上 Demo：https://free-oxr.somark.cn/ 免費 API：https://free-oxr.somark.cn/api/v1 有更多生產級文件解析需求的團隊，也可以瞭解同一團隊打造、由獨立模型驅動的文件解析引擎 SoMark。 SoMark 官網：https://somark.cn/ 從 SoMark 到 OXR，這支團隊向開發者開放他們在長期探索與實踐中積累的寶貴經驗，正傳達了他們的價值取向：讓文件中的知識成為 AI 可用的高質量資料，進入更多真實業務場景。 item.title: Artificial Analysis v5 and the benchmarker's dilemma
item.abstract: Hill-climbing is easy, knowing what to hill-climb is hard. Making scores go up is expensive , but we have a much clearer playbook for it than we do for creating meaningful benchmarks at the true frontier of AI today. Independent evaluation of language models is under-appreciated in how hard of a task it is. These groups are not just taking current models and certifying their scores, which is a technically involved task. This is their job if AI progress is slow. When AI progress is as fast as it is, the technical details of the job are the routine work part of trying to put a single number on what makes for a good AI model today. The goal is to have a single number that is representative of current models, matching vibe checks, community sentiment, and scientific analysis, while being forward looking enough so that it’s not outdated in 3 months. Everyone building a benchmark faces a sort of paradox. You need your benchmark to reduce to one single number, so that it is easy to discuss, use in reports, and compare models, but every method of aggregating scores comes with meaningful trade-offs. The best scientists need to do this, everyone does. It’s a matter of creating aggregating metrics that you think are most fair, knowing there will always be imperfections. With the amount of money in the AI ecosystem today, the weight of independent evaluation is even higher – you dictate the winners and losers of a trillion dollar market. You also influence some of the models themselves, steering the shape of progress. This is a lot of pressure! My prompt for this article is Artificial Analysis’s recent update to their Intelligence Index, v5 . The AA index is the most prominent independent intelligence metric for the latest frontier models, followed in a distant second by Epoch AI’s Capabilities Index (ECI) . To date, all of these have been incredibly useful for the community and massively flawed! Language models are capable of so much today, and this scope of capabilities is growing quickly. Our era of singular intelligence indices should be phased out soon, but it will take a long time. A summary of AAv5 is below, from their blog post, where they describe it as “reflecting real-world usage today:” Intelligence Index v5 weights: ➤ Knowledge Work (25%): AA-Briefcase (15%), AutomationBench-AA (5%), and GDP.pdf (5%) ➤ Coding (25%): FrontierCode 2.0 (15%) and Terminal-Bench 4.0 (10%) ➤ Science (25%): Terminal-Bench-Science (15%) and CritPt v2 hard subset (10%) ➤ General (25%): AA-Omniscience v1.1 15% (10% accuracy, 5% non-hallucination) and HLE-Diamond (10%) Here’s the new ranking of models: The problem with trying to benchmark real-world usage today is that it is extremely jagged, just like the models. The most proven use-case is coding, where open models are far more competitive and likely to keep up. In knowledge work, I’m less confident in open models. At first glance, in aggregate, this definitely looks reasonable. Still, it shows signs of strain and confusion, as any benchmark will, with GPT 6.1 Terra beating Claude Fable 5.1. Today, some benchmarks measure the absolute frontier of capabilities, playing nicely in open-ended tasks through your favorite harness, which often does take a large model. Some other benchmarks measure certain skills that will be needed of a model in repetitive agentic tasks. I get the feeling that AA is tuning their benchmark more towards the former, a general agentic collaborator, but all of these behaviors overlap. This takes us to the plot going around that prompted me to write this, where they showed the balance of open vs. closed models on the new benchmark. This plot shows 8 closed models beating the best to-be open-weight model, Kimi K3.1 Pro (which isn’t colored blue). This benchmark is taking the opinion of trying to measure where frontier models are moving into, which grows the gap to open models. This is an okay decision to take, but over time as existing workflows of open models become key factors of the economy, it could become a benchmark that misses where the core economic engine of the industry is. Open models’ demise from this seems greatly exaggerated, but I do think the previous index was flattering the open weight models too strongly. Consider this plot from the Kimi K3.1 Pro launch — yes, the open models are strong and useful in some cases, but the best OpenAI and Anthropic models have been a major step ahead in their flexibility and reliability. Some of the evaluations in AAv5 that open models are most behind on are “science” evals like terminal-bench-science and CritPT v2 . Open models are behind, but the value proposition was never to compete truly at the frontier. The open model economy will be about Reducing domains with high market demand for inference to a commodity price of hardware. Allowing ownership of intelligence, specializing it to internal data, and controlling internal agents across many companies in the economy. Both of these take a very long time and are partially represented in benchmarks. The supply of compute is currently so low that open model providers also are raking in solid margins – when this shrinks, we will know the system is starting to work. The same goes for diffusion into enterprises, it’s not clear what the exact ceiling on it is because of the difficult ML expertise that is needed to build evaluations and do post-training today. At the next major model cycle, say in 2-3 months with GLM 6 or Kimi 3.5, I expect the leading open model labs to make substantial steps on this index, again surprising many observers. This is a cycle we have been on for years now. I’ve written many times about how open models keep up with the frontier, and a summary is that: The best open models do benchmax a little. The worst open models benchmax a lot (but don’t get a ton of attention anyways). The best open models are a bit narrower in which capabilities they cover, as seen above with their gap on scientific domains. The open model labs are working to address this, but I think it could be come a strategic error to not focus. There’s a more nuanced version of explanations of the performance gap today, where so many of the gains in training are coming from having RL environments with distributions close to the evaluations (a longer analysis on this is here ). Keeping up with rapid progress across multiple domains requires a sophisticated RL stack that not all the open model labs may possess. Some may be reliant on buying data that has moderate lead times as well. Another part of this announcement is shifting to “private benchmarks”, where the prompts are not public, as a sign that open labs are benchmaxxing. This sort of analysis has been done before , and fits with my above theory on how open labs benchmax. It is easier to create training data to support an evaluation when you know the shape of it, but the task isn’t impossible with hidden data. All in, this is a change that directionally I think is defensible, but it’s not unanimous. For example, you’re putting complete trust in the private benchmark builder, as you no longer get the benefit of the community finding issues in the benchmark and pushing the benchmark to improve itself – which happens a lot! There is enough money on the line, where I’d rather see transparency in benchmarking and enabling many eyes to find bugs. The final point I need to make, which does flatter the closed labs, is that the likes of Anthropic and OpenAI moved on from caring about these indices months, or even years, ago. Their focus is to a large majority on supporting internal uses – like AI R&D automation – and the use-cases of customers who are spending billions of dollars. Yes, they have team members hill climbing on other capabilities to unlock new markets, but these behaviors are to a minority extent driven by public benchmarks.

item.abstract: Physical RSI第一站！便利店打工“人”自己進化，物理AI飛輪啟動了 衡宇 2026-10-27 16:46:12 來源： 量子位 無人在環進店實測啃下長尾場景 衡宇 發自 凹非寺 量子位 | 公眾號 QbitAI 因為貨架上的小尺寸掛鉤被價格標籤牌擋住了一部分，進便利店打工的機器人君第一次嘗試掛貨……撲了個空。 換作以往，這時候就必須由人工工程師出馬，先排查問題，再調整程式、補充資料，讓機器人重新練習一遍。 但機器人君有點不一樣。 它自己琢磨出了新辦法。 它回看此前的執行記錄，發現頭部相機的視角解析度不足，加上標籤牌遮擋，很難看清小掛鉤的位置。 於是，Agent調整了策略，讓左手先靠近目標，用腕部相機補上一個近距離視角，確認位置後，再由右手完成掛貨。 更值得一提的是，剛才機器人君不僅自己發現了問題所在、尋得了解法， 還把這套有效經驗默默積累了下來，以備不時之需。 這套讓機器人在工作中發現問題、調整策略、積累經驗的機制，背後是 智元最新發布的具身 Agent框架Genie Master。 這也是智元近期掀起的“AI WAVE”系列技術釋出的第四彈——這一次，智元在業界把Physical RSI （具身遞迴自進化） 搬進了真實便利店業務流。 在Genie Master的加持下，智元精靈G2機器人在真實便利店環境執行任務的過程中，已經可以不依賴人工示範與除錯，自主分析失敗原因、調整策略、沉澱經驗， 實現 “無人在環”的持續自我改進。 這是行業首次跳出模擬環境與實驗室設定 （toy setting） ，在真實業務場景中跑通並驗證了 Physical RSI。 Genie Master這套自主進化的閉環到底是怎麼玩起來的？它又能為機器人的批次上崗，帶來哪些顛覆性的改變？ Genie Master是什麼？ 要搞清楚這臺機器人為什麼能“自己悟道”，首先得看看它背後的Genie Master到底是個啥。 簡單來說，Genie Master是 一套具身 Agent框架，其核心任務是連線上層Agent的推理能力與底層機器人的動作執行能力。 它不僅讓Agent能夠順暢地呼叫機器人的各項能力、理解真實的物理執行反饋，還能根據任務進展持續組織行動和針對性練習。 一旦機器人在實際工作中暴露出了能力短板，這個問題就會直接進入自主改進流程。 不難看出，Genie Master想要重點構建 機器人部署之後的持續改進機制 ——這其中既涉及任務執行當下的判斷與動態調整，也涵蓋了事後的經驗沉澱和底層動作策略更新。 智元之所以提出這個框架，是因為它看到了行業長期以來的落地痛點。 行內人都知道，機器人進入真實商業場景後，難免遇到訓練階段沒有覆蓋的長尾情況。 執行失敗、動作不穩定，或者某項任務耗時過長，都可能需要工程師介入排查，再通過調整程式、補充示範資料或訓練模型來改善表現。 場景越多，任務越複雜，研發和維護的工作量也會隨之增加。 如果每一種新需求都等著人工從頭排查和除錯，迭代速度就會受限，更難以跨場景大規模鋪開落地。 一言以蔽之， 具身智慧要想真正大規模用起來，就必須從依賴人工示範的 “被動微調”，轉向機器人自主發現問題、解決問題的“自進化模式”。 Genie Master希望將其中一部分工作交給Agent。 通過把問題診斷、組織練習和結果評估都交由Agent來操盤，Genie Master支援機器人自主習得新能力，從而 大幅縮短從 “客戶提出一項新需求”到“機器人掌握這項新本領”之間的研發週期。 除了開頭提到的掛鉤補貨，在真實便利店的實測中，搭載Genie Master的機器人還展現出了更多應對複雜局面的能力。 據智元介紹，Genie Master團隊已將取貨、補貨、清潔、異常恢復和多機協作納入統一工作流，探索機器人在真實業務中的持續改進閉環。 閒時自己“加練”，具身Agent框架打通大腦與小腦 讓機器人在工作中自我進化，思路並不難。 但在此之前，為什麼這件事只停留在實驗室的討論裡，幾乎沒人真正在現實業務中做起來、做出來？ 究其原因，無論是上層的經驗沉澱，還是底層的策略內化，都必須建立在一個極其硬核的基礎之上—— 上層推理 “大腦”的引導，必須能精準落實為動作；底層執行“小腦”的結果，也必須能即時反饋給大腦。 為了打通這條任督二脈，Genie Master拿出了它的關鍵設計之一： 具身執行協議 EEP （Embodied Execution Protocol） 。 EEP為Agent與物理世界建立了一套統一介面，主要涵蓋了四類核心介面： 能力介面 ：讓Agent清楚知道機器人當前有哪些能力可以呼叫； 引導介面 ：讓Agent能夠向底層動作執行端傳遞具體的空間提示、物體參考和細粒度語言要求； 反饋介面：讓Agent即時瞭解機器人執行動作後的真實物理情況； 連續性介面：讓系統能夠持續追蹤機器人叢集的任務進度、分工依賴，支援動態排程以及中斷後的任務接續。 通過EEP協議，並配合時序對齊 （Temporal Alignment） 等協同設計，上層Agent可以根據執行結果隨時動態調整引導；而底層的基座動作策略 （Action Policy） 則能結合當前觀測和Agent的要求去精準執行動作，並即時返回觀測與子任務狀態。 在具身智慧系統中，只有把推理、執行和反饋真正擰成一股繩，自我進化才不是空中樓閣 。 EEP承擔的正是這條互動鏈路中的關鍵介面作用，為後續的經驗積累和策略更新打下了地基。 地基打牢之後，機器人在部署態下的“自卷”日常就開始了。 在便利店的正常工作流中，當機器人發現某些任務反覆失敗、執行不穩或者耗時過長，也就是暴露出了“能力缺口”時，Agent並不會坐視不管。 它會主動利用便利店的空閒時間，組織機器人針對這些薄弱環節進行“自主加練”。 練什麼、怎麼練、練完之後結果合不合格、遇到異常怎麼恢復並重試，全由Agent一手張羅。真實的部署環境，就這樣源源不斷地為機器人提供著“接下來該練什麼、該改什麼”的實戰依據。 一條路線積累經驗，一條路線更新動作策略 既然已經在真實場景裡把“發現問題”和“自主加練”張羅起來了，那麼機器人又是如何把練出來的成果，真正長成自己身上的本事呢？ 在這裡，Genie Master採取了“雙管齊下”的策略。 一條路線叫 Harness RSI ，負責積累經驗；另一條路線叫 Policy RSI ，負責更新動作策略。 先來看 Harness RSI 。 它的核心邏輯是在保持模型權重和已有工具介面不變的前提下，主要通過最佳化提示詞 （Prompt） 、記憶 （Memory） 和執行規則來改善後續的任務表現。 在日常推理執行的過程中，機器人會把成功和失敗的例子“隨做隨記”；隨後再通過每日的非同步反思與記憶整合，把這些執行記錄轉化為更有效的引導、完成判定、異常恢復和協作規則，像寫“錯題本”一樣納入長期記憶中，並在後續按任務和場景需要逐步載入。 回看文章開頭那個“便利店掛貨”的案例，其實就是Harness RSI在發力。 最開始，那個小掛鉤任務的成功率很低。但Agent在回溯了失敗記錄後診斷出了病根，即“頭部相機視角解析度不足，加上標籤牌遮擋，導致機器人無法準確識別小尺寸掛鉤的位置”。 於是，Agent把“先用左手腕部相機湊近補視角、確認後再用右手掛貨”的新解法寫進了可執行的經驗裡，後續再遇到類似情況，就能直接調取經驗、從容應對。 “錯題本”外，為了滿足真機部署對低延遲、高穩定性的嚴苛要求，有些能力必須變成機器人的“肌肉記憶”。 這就輪到 Policy RSI 登場了。 Policy RSI會將機器人在自主執行、人工接管示範以及異常恢復過程中產生的資料，統統收集整理起來，通過篩選、加權和目標重標等方式提高資料質量，再使用監督學習、模仿學習或強化學習去直接更新底層的動作策略模型 （Action Policy） ，讓改進真正保留在模型參數裡。 假設機器人在店裡做“外賣打包防纏繞”這一任務，處理提帶纏繞、執行回撤和異常恢復時產生的資料，經過篩選和處理後，可以用於後續動作策略訓練，幫助模型改善類似任務的執行表現。 通過Policy RSI，機器人得以從一次次真實的執行經歷中吸收養分，獲得更穩定的執行力與更準確的指令跟隨能力。 需要說明的是，不是說從此完全不需要人工參與了，Policy RSI仍會使用人工接管示範等資料，動作策略的更新也需要經過資料處理和模型訓練。 更妙的是， 這兩條路線並不是各自為戰，而是相互咬合、形成了一個越轉越快的飛輪 —— Harness RSI負責積累和組織經驗，幫助系統分析失敗原因、選擇練習方式，並改善後續執行； Policy RSI則將經過處理的執行資料用於動作策略訓練，讓有效經驗有機會沉澱為更穩定的動作能力。 兩條路線相互促進，形成從真實業務執行、發現能力缺口、自主練習，到經驗沉澱和策略更新的閉環。智元希望藉此讓每一輪積累的經驗，都能幫助系統更有效地診斷問題、選擇練習和利用資料。 讓提升能力的能力也持續進化 ， 在相同投入下獲得更大的能力增量 ，這正是“遞迴自進化 （RSI） ”的真正威力所在。 從“出廠即定型”到“越幹越能幹” 跳出便利店，站在整個具身智慧產業的視角來看 ，智元Genie Master所探索的方向，正在推開一扇新的大門。 首先，在研發效率上 ，它徹底打破了以往機器人能力“出廠即定型”的枷鎖，將其轉向了“部署中持續生長”的新範式。 當AI的新解法能夠自己在現場長成機器人的新本領，從客戶提出新需求到機器人掌握新技能的交付週期將被大幅壓縮。 其次，在商業化落地上 ，這也算清楚了一筆經濟賬。 當機器人在真實作業中“越幹越能幹”，同一套能力便會在部署中不斷增厚。 未來向更多門店、更多跨行業場景複製時，後續部署與研發的邊際成本將持續下探。 而這條不斷降低的成本曲線，正是具身智慧走向大規模商業化落地的核心前提。 回看智元自10月22日起啟動的“AI WAVE”系列釋出，作為其中的第四項內容，Genie Master在智元全棧具身AI的整體佈局中起著關鍵的承上啟下作用——它將底層基座模型與全棧AI能力延伸並紮根到了真實的商業部署態中。 當然，技術架構講得再精彩，最終還是要靠實戰表現來說話。 俗話說得好，是騾子是馬，拉出來遛遛。 11月2日 ，智元計劃開啟一場全網圍觀的“24小時便利店直播”。 屆時，將有6臺精靈G2機器人連續上崗，在沒有劇本的真實便利店營業中，接受嚴苛的轉正考核。 版權所有，未經授權不得以任何形式轉載及使用，違者必究。 RSI 智元機器人 物理AI 衡宇 item.title: Git for the US Code
item.abstract:
A programmer can point at any line of code and see who wrote it, when, and what the file looked like on any past day. A lawyer reading a federal statute usually cannot, at least not without an afternoon in the notes at the foot of the section. But why shouldn't they have the same, convenient system of record? It is especially relevant given that so much first-pass legal research now runs through language models, which are often unable to utilise the proper lineage of a law, handcuffing its ability to offer interpretation. The US code Outside the titles Congress has enacted as positive law, the code is only prima facie evidence of the law, and the Statutes at Large govern where the two differ. [ 1 ] The Office of the Law Revision Counsel publishes it as a series of release points, each current through a named public law, and keeps reorganising it; a bill to enact title 41 as positive law was introduced in September 2025. [ 2 ] Which public law wrote a sentence is recorded in amendment notes, in prose. When a change took effect is often in a separate effective-date note, and where Congress said nothing the default rule is that a law takes effect on the day it is enacted. [ 3 ] The definition of a small business debtor in 11 USC § 1182(1) shows how far apart those answers can be. It was created in 2019 with the existing small business debt limit. [ 4 ] The CARES Act raised the limit to $7.5 million in March 2020 as a temporary measure, later extended to March 2022. [ 5 ] , [ 6 ] That increase lapsed on 27 March 2022, and on 21 June 2022 Congress restored it for two more years, for cases commenced on or after 27 March 2020 and still pending, which reached back over the gap. [ 7 ] The higher limit expired again in June 2024, and after the triennial adjustment in April 2025 it stands at $3,424,000. [ 8 ] , [ 9 ] For a case filed in May 2022, the release point printed at the time gives the lower limit, and only a later Act changes the answer. A history that is useful to a lawyer has to carry the text, the date each change took force, and the scope of any law that reaches back. A study from the Technical University of Munich this year found two failures in models answering questions on German statutes: they apply rules that were superseded after their training cutoff, and they prefer the newer provision even when an older one governs the facts. One model answered 24% of post-cutoff questions correctly on its own and 87% when the relevant statutory text was retrieved for it, and the authors conclude that temporal validity has to be treated as a hard constraint. [ 10 ] Other recent work trains search agents to respect the date a question is about, with large gains in consistency. [ 11 ] Asking a model to produce the old text does not solve this. When the same Munich group had a model apply German amending laws to earlier versions, the output looked 93–99% similar to the official text, but only half of single amendments and a fifth of chains of amendments matched exactly, and experts found legally significant errors in the near misses. [ 12 ] The history has to be checkable. For each pair of release points from 2017 onward, we took the public laws enacted in between, carried out their amending instructions on the older text in date order, and compared the result with the newer version. Of 365 changes across the nine titles, 361 reproduced the next release point exactly. The other four are shown with a label saying how far they could be confirmed. Each change then carries the law and the date it took effect: 261 took effect on enactment by default, 72 by an effective-date note and 29 by a date in the amendment itself. One depends on an agency determination that may never come, and we leave it out of the text rather than guess. With that record, the reader can answer the questions lawyers ask. You pick a date and get the text in force on it, with the words that read differently today marked. Each phrase is coloured by the Act that wrote it. A change to a defined term lists every other provision that uses it, and you can follow a section to see what has changed since your last visit. Limits It does not yet show a later law’s reach back on the earlier dates it covers, so for a case filed in the 2022 gap it shows the lower limit without warning that the June 2022 Act changed the answer. Effective-date notes are read by pattern, and unusual wording falls back to the date of enactment. Each change links to the law’s own words, and for anything that matters the original should be read. We're also still thinking about the right form factor this should take. item.title: Dayjob: Tax – evaluating AI agents on 50 professional tax assignments
item.abstract:
Table of contents Case Study Llama Analysis of Individual writings Appendix Anna was planning to sell her condo. She had moved out in August 2024 and wanted to know whether closing in October 2026 or January 2027 would be better for taxes. An AI agent reviewed both options and correctly concluded that either date would satisfy the residence requirement for a tax break worth up to $250,000 in excluded gains. But it left out an important deadline. Under the usual rules, homeowners must have lived in a property for at least two of the five years before selling it to qualify for the exclusion. Because Anna moved out in August 2024, she would stop satisfying that requirement around the end of August 2027. If her sale was delayed beyond August 2027, she could lose eligibility. Across five attempts, Astra never identified the deadline. Opus identified it in all five attempts. The agent evaluated the proposed dates correctly, but its advice left Anna unaware of a deadline that could affect a major financial decision. A tax adviser should recognize consequential issues even when the client doesn't know to ask about them. This is the kind of professional judgment we're testing with DAYJOB: Tax , the latest addition to Surge AI's DAYJOB benchmark family . Introducing DAYJOB: Tax DAYJOB evaluates AI agents on professional tax assignments requiring specialized expertise, complex materials, and decisions that aren't fully specified in the initial instructions. Our earlier releases covered Healthcare and Finance. DAYJOB: Tax extends that work into tax preparation, compliance, and advisory services. The benchmark contains 50 environments across eight areas of tax practice. Agents receive client requests and supporting records, then produce tax returns, workpapers, technical reviews, or client advice. These assignments test professional judgment alongside tax knowledge, calculations, retrieval, and instruction following. Agents must decide what deserves investigation, resolve conflicting evidence, recognize when information is insufficient, and carry those decisions into their final work. Results: Leaderboard and Pareto Frontiers Claude Sonnet 5.5 leads with a 10.8% pass rate on the DAYJOB: Tax leaderboard , followed by Claude Fable 5.1 at 9.6% and Claude Opus 5.5 at 9.2%. We report pass@1 at a 95% rubric threshold. An attempt passes when it satisfies at least 95% of the task's criteria, which assess calculations, supporting evidence, consequential issues, and the completed deliverable. Performance versus cost We also compared model performance against average cost per trial. Claude Sonnet 5.5 and Opus 5.5 occupy the high-performance end of the measured Pareto frontier. The breadth of professional tax work DAYJOB: Tax covers eight areas, each requiring different rules, records, and expertise: Individual and family tax Small-business tax Partnerships Property and investments Estates, gifts, and trusts International tax Corporate transactions Tax review and disputes Some assignments require complete filing packages with supporting workpapers. Others ask agents to investigate transactions, review previous filings, or prepare advice about decisions clients haven't yet made. What's inside the assignments? The benchmark contains 1,789 workspace files , with a median of 30 per assignment and as many as 123. These include 1,487 PDFs, 117 Excel workbooks, 38 Word documents, and additional emails, images, CSVs, JSON records, and text files. The workspaces include filed and draft tax returns, K-1s, W-2s, IRS notices, general ledgers, payroll records, contracts, and correspondence. They also contain the less standardized evidence that tax professionals routinely work with. One assignment includes a photograph of a handwritten receipt for merchandise purchased for resale . The agent must read the item descriptions and amounts, reconcile them with spending records, and determine how the purchases affect inventory and cost of goods sold. Another assignment involves an industrial silo-services company whose client assumes it operates only in Alabama. But its field dispatch log shows crews working across five states . The job locations, crew sizes, and days on site provide evidence relevant to the company's multistate tax obligations. Other environments are similarly varied. One involves a cross-border household whose Polish employment and property records must be reconciled with cryptocurrency exchange exports, wallet histories, and historical purchase lots. Created and reviewed by tax experts DAYJOB tasks begin with real-world professional workflows. Tax experts turn these situations into realistic assignments, developing the supporting records, expected outcomes, and grading criteria. Each task undergoes a three-layer expert review for correctness, completeness, and solvability. Tax experts bring experience across corporate taxation, partnerships, individual returns, trusts, and multistate compliance. Their backgrounds include: Corporate and private-equity taxation: A tax attorney with over 10 years of experience at PwC, Deloitte, and Exxon, covering tax planning, compliance, audits, and controversy. Partnership and corporate taxation: A Baker Tilly Tax Director with experience at PwC, Moss Adams, and Windes, specializing in complex partnership allocations, consolidated corporate returns, REITs, and high-net-worth clients. Real estate and individual taxation: A tax professional with experience at Deloitte and EY, specializing in real-estate partnerships, individual taxation, and trusts. A retirement plan built on an unverified assumption A separating couple asked an AI agent how to divide their Roth IRA and 401(k). Opus 5.5 told them they weren't legally married and recommended keeping their accounts separate, with a cash payment to even out the balances. It opened one response: You aren't legally married, so neither account can be split without triggering taxes and penalties. But the couple's own records raised doubts about that conclusion. Although they now lived in Florida, where new common-law marriages generally aren't recognized, they had previously lived together in Texas and held a ceremony in Colorado. Texas recognizes informal marriages under certain conditions, and a valid marriage established elsewhere may remain valid in Florida. That distinction could change the tax consequences of dividing their retirement accounts. Across all five attempts, Opus based its recommendations around the assumption that the couple was unmarried , even when it acknowledged uncertainty. Astra recognized the need to verify their marital status in four of five attempts. One response advised: We first need to confirm your legal marital status. The client asked how to divide the accounts. The agent needed to establish whether they were married before recommending a course of action. The evidence that should have prompted that investigation was already in the files. Where DAYJOB: Tax fits Most existing tax benchmarks begin with a defined problem: a legal question to answer, a return to calculate, or missing taxpayer information to collect. These evaluations measure important capabilities, but much of a tax professional's work involves figuring out what the problem actually is. Clients provide incomplete instructions, records contain conflicting evidence, and consequential issues may never appear in the original request. DAYJOB tests whether agents can handle that end-to-end responsibility , including identifying issues the client overlooked, evaluating conflicting evidence, and deciding what needs to be done in the first place. TaxBench Can the model answer a difficult tax question? TaxBench evaluates 114 tax questions across multiple specialties, each with a defined problem and grading rubric. DAYJOB also asks whether the client asked the right question. Anna wants to compare two dates for selling her condo.

item.abstract: Personal Agent走向真實任務，螞蟻百靈開源 Ling-3.1-flash-1019 量子位的朋友們 2026-10-28 12:04:48 來源： 量子位 10月28 日，螞蟻集團旗下百靈大模型正式開源 Ling-3.1-flash-1019。 10月28 日，螞蟻集團旗下百靈大模型正式開源 Ling-3.1-flash-1019。新版本在 Ling-3.1-flash 基礎上進一步訓練最佳化，在智慧指數Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index v4.3.2 中獲得44分，較上一版本提升3分。與此同時，百靈同步開源其基礎模型 Ling-3.1-flash-base，為長程任務所需的知識、推理和計算效率打好基礎。 據瞭解，Ling-3.1-flash-1019 版本面向 Personal Agent 場景，進一步提升了模型處理複雜工作流和多步驟任務的表現。從測評具體來看，新版本在複雜知識工作AA-Briefcase 中的得分從約1400 Elo提升至1524 Elo，GDPval-AA從約1618 Elo提升至1644 Elo；流程自動化AutomationBench-AA得分從62%提升至68%；科學問題求解CritPt得分從18%提升至26%，SciCode得分從54%提升至57%。 記者注意到，百靈本次模型迭代開源與靈光 2.0 息息相關。就在 10 月 27日，靈光 2.0 升級為「能管事的個人AI助理」，依託跨會話記憶、長程任務排程與獨立雲主機等能力，靈光可以在使用者授權範圍內更主動地跟進任務、持續管理生活中的複雜事務，即使使用者退出對話，相關任務也能繼續執行。這背後對模型能力提出了新要求。 從回答問題到持續辦事，模型需要哪些新能力？ 與即時問答不同，個人智慧體需要圍繞一個目標持續工作，這既需要產品具備記憶和任務排程機制，也需要底層模型能夠理解目標、使用工具、處理新資訊並推進任務。 靈光2.0，呈現了這類能力在個人生活中的應用。 例如，規劃一趟旅行，不只是生成一份行程攻略，還需要結合出發時間跟進天氣、預約和行前準備；面對雙11購物需求，則要按照預算、規格和個人偏好篩選商品、整理清單，並持續關注價格變化，在符合約定條件時提醒使用者。 圍繞這些需求，百靈持續通過模型訓練和應用反饋，探索 Personal Agent 所需的能力。Ling-3.1-flash-base 在設計初期就將這些需求納入考慮，模型採用混合線性 MoE 架構，總參數量約560B，每個 Token 啟用約25B參數，在模型容量、長序列處理和單步計算開銷之間取得平衡，為後續面向真實任務的訓練提供基礎。 在 8 個領域共 47 項 benchmark 測試中，Ling-3.1-flash-base 在 32 項上超越了 DeepSeek-V4-Pro-Base 和 MiMo-V2.5-Pro-Base，取得最高分。其中，知識理解、邏輯推理、程式碼、數學與長上下文評測，對應著個人助理處理複雜事務所需的多項基礎能力，成為處理複雜任務的重要起點。據瞭解，Ling-3.1-flash-base以 BF16 基礎權重、MIT 許可證向開發者開放，開發者可以基於自身的知識、流程和工具開展繼續預訓練、領域適配及後訓練。 在基礎能力之上，Ling-3.1-flash 及後續的 1019 版本通過後訓練，持續強化推理、工具使用和多步驟執行能力，持續提升模型在實際工作流中的表現。記者注意到，百靈從 Base 到後訓練模型，研發重點逐步延伸到如何遵循目標、使用工具和推進任務。 據瞭解，圍繞個人事務中的多模態資訊處理需求，百靈基於 Ling-3.1-flash 訓練了視覺語言模型 Ling-3.1-flash-VL，在既有推理、規劃和工具使用能力的基礎上增加視覺理解，目前已先行應用於靈光，後續將對外發布。 從真實任務中來，到真實應用中去 目前，百靈正逐步完善 Personal Agent 所需的模型能力。模型層面的能力演進，也正在應用中得到進一步驗證和探索。據瞭解， Ling-3.1-flash 已基於靈光、阿福醫生版等應用場景的需求與反饋開展對齊訓練，持續提升模型在專業表達和溝通等方面的能力。 “從真實任務中來，到真實應用中去。”百靈表示，希望通過模型研發與應用實踐的持續迴圈，提升模型理解目標、保持任務狀態和應對變化的能力，並且將持續通過開源與開發者共同探索更多應用可能。 記者注意到，不同於單純追求模型參數規模，百靈更注重讓基礎模型能力進入真實流程，完成真實任務。今年下半年以來，百靈圍繞開放開源和真實場景加速模型迭代和發展。 此前，百靈基於新一代基座模型Ling-3.0-flash，分別推出金融增強模型Ling-3.0-flash-Fin和醫療增強模型Ling-3.0-flash-Sante，將基礎模型能力進一步帶入真實專業場景。 其中，Ling-3.0-flash-Fin（總參數124B、啟用5.1B）讓AI進入真實投研任務流，打通從找資料、做分析到形成研究成果的完整任務鏈，在高難度投研任務中比肩3T級前沿模型，金融Agent綜合表現達到開源領先；Ling-3.0-flash-Sante則將“高智效比”帶入醫療場景，以124B參數規模在1.6T以下模型中取得最優表現，整體效能與多款旗艦模型相當。 item.title: [AINews] Anthropic ends Coding Interviews: "Hunger beats tenure"
item.abstract: Several midsize headlines today; on top of some impressive Math verification , Google Genie and Artificial Analysis and FrontierCode all shipped major version bumps of their top offerings, all of which have been AINews title stories in the past, but are mostly annual incremental improvements. Past guest Felix Reiseberg gets the headline today for coming out and charting the path forward for junior engineers : “ Hunger beats tenure” This month, I laid the traditional coding interview to rest. As a hiring manager at Anthropic, I stopped asking candidates to do them… …There’s no more point in giving you a little React challenge than there is in quizzing people about assembly; Claude is now better at both. Our most impactful builders are successful regardless of how good they are at these tests. Pick business impact over backlog : In pre-AI-coding 2011, Patrick McKenzie wrote “engineers are hired to create business value, not to program things.” Pick a radical idea : Come up with a few ideas that would, if successful, dramatically improve the chances that your organization achieves those goals. Be ambitious! Build it over a weekend : I have seen small groups and solo engineers fly past the usual process of writing product requirements documents (PRDs), getting buy-in, and lobbying for time with designers or product managers by building a working prototype. Focus on one good idea : In my experience, junior people often make the mistake of cramming multiple ideas into a single prototype , hiding three excellent ideas among 20 bad ones. Lean into your fresh perspective : If you’re working on something user-facing, you have a unique amount of empathy for users and thus a much better sense for how the product works or doesn’t work for them. Get web search results as clean, structured Markdown, using roughly 50% fewer tokens than JSON on average. Easily integrate Markdown search results into your AI workflows across 100+ SerpApi APIs! Genie 4: DeepMind's Real-Time World Model Adds Audio, Physics and Gemini Planning Launch : Google DeepMind introduced Genie 4, its "most realistic and interactive world model yet." Users can explore generated environments in real time and steer events, camera angles and actions with text ( GDM , Sundar Pichai , Demis Hassabis ). Architecture : The model is built on Gemini Omni. Gemini runs in the loop to plan multi-step events and keep scenes coherent ( features , Eli Collins ). Native audio : It generates ambient sound, music and real-time dialogue with characters, a first for Genie ( Shlomi Fruchter ). Physics and photorealism : DeepMind claims aerodynamics, collisions and natural human motion. Genie 3's worlds were "too static," and Genie 4 responds to prompted events mid-generation ( Fruchter ). Robotics angle : DeepMind positions Genie 4 as a step toward safe virtual environments for testing agents and robots. Demos : Gemini 3.8 Flash decomposes tasks, checks each step and replans as the scene changes. A Gemini 4 Argon + Genie 4 experiment simulates an Apollo humanoid playing checkers ( summary ). Availability : The research preview is open to trusted testers now. Google AI Ultra subscribers will get access next via Project Genie, followed by early-access partners through the Gemini API and AI Studio, which marks Genie's first API availability ( Logan Kilpatrick , waitlist ). Early-access impressions : Users with early access describe prompting a "neogothic brutalist city," then adding dragons and an NPC live. They call it "not flawless" but a large leap over Genie 3 ( Ethan Mollick , venturetwins , Riley Goodside ). AI for Math and Science: CFSG Formalized, ETH Disproof Claims Axiom formalizes CFSG : Axiom announced a complete Lean auto-formalization of the Classification of Finite Simple Groups. The original proof spans about 15,000 pages across roughly 500 papers by more than 100 mathematicians ( Axiom , Kevin Weil ). Process : An agent swarm produced about 50M lines of Lean in 24 days. Agents claimed tasks, reviewed each other's work and merged through GitHub, with human guidance, and reportedly fixed hundreds of errata in the published proof ( omarsar0 , kimmonismus ). Context : Researchers note it displaces the four-color theorem as the largest computer-verified proof. Few humans understand the full CFSG proof ( hyhieu226 , Stella Biderman ). Exponential Time Hypothesis : OpenAI announced new results in harmonic analysis, complexity theory and QFT, including a claimed refutation of ETH, with materials in its openai/math repo ( Romain Huet , Dan ). Anthropic's parallel claim : Anthropic reportedly says Claude independently disproved ETH, finding the key algorithm on Oct 16 with "14M output tokens and no human input." PSI also claims progress on five open quantum physics problems with computer-checked proofs ( Rundown roundup ). Physics follow-up : A Yang-Mills Working Group published a statement interpreting an AI result related to the existence of quantum Yang-Mills theory ( KITP ). Smaller results : Ten Claude agents proved in Lean that seven electrons on a sphere settle into a pentagonal bipyramid, a case of the Thomson problem ( Vals ). Separately, a Stanford study had 29 experts rate AI-proposed research problems and judged about one-third "interesting" ( Percy Liang ). Independent Evals: AA Index v5, FrontierCode 2.0 and GPT-6.1 Terra Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index v5 : 60% of the index now comes from private or held-out sets ( announcement ). Composition : It adds FrontierCode 2.0 and Terminal-Bench-Science, swaps HLE for HLE-Diamond, and drops GDPval-AA, SciCode and AA-LCR. Four categories carry equal 25% weights ( weights ). Leaders : Claude Opus 5.5 (max) scores 58, GPT-6 Astra 57, GPT-6.1 Sol 55 and Gemini 4 Argon 50. Open-weights gap : The gap widens from 3 to 12 points. Kimi K3.1 Pro, whose weights are unreleased, scores 46. DeepSeek V4.1 Flash 1017 and GLM-5.3 score 32, below Claude Haiku 5.5's 36. Cost : GPT-6.1 Terra costs $0.96 per task and Claude Fable 5.1 $13.04 among the top 10. Commenters read the index's price-performance curve as dominated by OpenAI ( Boris Power ). FrontierCode 2.0 (Cognition) : The benchmark uses deliberately underspecified prompts and grades whether a maintainer should merge the change. The top score is 45% ( launch ). Ranking shifts : Muse Wonder 1.0 and Gemini 4 Argon lead DeepSWE v1.1 but land mid-pack here ( thread ). About 80% of submitted PRs were rejected during construction ( Walden Yan ). Lab gap : The top 20 are all OpenAI and Anthropic models plus Grok 4.7, with DeepSeek V4.1 Flash at #52 ( scaling01 ). DeepSeek 1017 gains 8.9% over 0910 ( teortaxes ). GPT-6.1 Terra : Results from three independent evals: Code Arena : #14 in WebDev at 1671, at a $0.40 median cost per task, 28% below GPT-5.6 Terra ( Arena ). Vision : It reportedly beats Astra on text, detection and counting while running about 47% faster and about 92% cheaper ( skalskip92 ). ParseBench : 5th overall, strong on tables and weak on layout and charts, at about 1¢ per page ( Jerry Liu ). MAI-Image-2.7-Preview : Microsoft's image-editing model ranks #2 on AA-Image-Editing behind GPT Image 2.5 Sunburst and #1 on 4 of 7 editing actions ( AA ). It is #3 in Arena's Image Edit leaderboard at 1470 (+45 over 2.6) and available for editing only in MAI Playground ( Arena ). Ling 3.1 Flash 1019 : The open model (560B total / 25B active, 1M context, MIT license) scores 44 on AA Index v4.3, up from 41 ( AA ). Pricing : $0.30/$0.90 per million input/output tokens. Token usage : It uses more than 40% more output tokens per task (145k), for $1.49 per task. Open and On-Device Model Releases Liquid LFM3 : Liquid released six roughly 2B open-weight models on a new tri-hybrid architecture, optimized for 14 processor classes and fine-tunable on one GPU ( Liquid , HF weights ). Lineup : LFM3-1.
